title: Tayammum case cards
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y7 lesson 22 (Pupil PDF worksheet: tayammum case cards)
intro: Lesson 22: Tayammum: purification when there is no water. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Qur'an, al-Ma'idah 5:6 (translation of the meaning)
paras: ... and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you.

panels.title: When is it allowed?
points: No water, or not enough to drink and wash
Water would harm: illness or a wound
Until water can be used again

parts.text: Strike clean earth once with both palms
Wipe the backs of the hands

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A valid tayammum, standing in place of wudu or ghusl

questions.q: Camping with only enough water to drink.

questions.a: Allowed for that part (water would harm it).

questions.q: Cold weather, but water is available.
questions.a: Not allowed: warm the water and make wudu.
Use water if there is any; if not, tayammum.

keywords.def: purifying with clean earth when water cannot be used
a concession: an easier rule allowed for a reason

questions.q: Explain how tayammum shows that Islam is a religion of ease.
questions.a: When water cannot be used, Allah allows clean earth instead, so a Muslim can always pray (5:6).

questions.q: Which parts are wiped in tayammum?
Case cards on the pupil PDF: decide whether tayammum is allowed and why (camping with only drinking water; a burn on the hand; cold weather but water available; a long flight).
questions.a: Allowed: drinking water only; burn (for that part). Not allowed: cold but water usable (warm it). Flight: use water if available, else tayammum

questions.q: Extend: does tayammum need water later to 'make up' the prayer?
questions.a: No: a prayer prayed with valid tayammum is valid.

questions.q: Stretch: compare wudu and tayammum in a table (when, parts, what ends it).
questions.a: Wudu: water, four parts; tayammum: earth, face and hands; both end with what breaks wudu; tayammum also ends when water is found

questions.q: Sara has a plaster cast on her arm and the doctor says no water. What does she do?
options: Wudu for the rest and tayammum or wipe for the cast
questions.a: A) Wudu for the rest and tayammum or wipe for the cast. Scholars allow wiping over a cast or tayammum; salah is never dropped.

questions.q: Think again: can someone in hospital still pray?
questions.a: Yes: with tayammum or wiping, and in whatever position they can.
